summary: Applied the sign-poisoning fix to tapit-attest verifyEnvelope per DESIGN.md §11. Switched to quorum-of-good semantics: at least one valid signature suffices, invalid signatures are reported in errors but no longer poison the result, and duplicate bad rows for an otherwise-valid signer are dropped from errors. Added two regression tests covering the relayer-appended junk signature vector and the duplicate-bad-row case. Bumped tapit-attest version to 0.1.1-wallet.0 to mark wallet-side divergence. Operator is in manual mode (AppCommander down) and asked me to keep going until I judged the design was ready to start Phase 1 code. My judgement: ready.

why.text: DESIGN.md §11 named the sign-poisoning fix as the one-time pre-Phase-1 library cherry-pick. The bug was live in tapit-attest/src/core/keys.ts verifyEnvelope: returning valid=false the moment any signature failed let a malicious relayer poison a genuine envelope by appending a junk signature. The upstream library timeline in the uploaded zip already had the fix in quorum-of-good shape; this session adapts that fix to the wallet's bundled VerifyResult shape so no caller of verifyEnvelope needs to change. Caller audit confirmed: sync.ts, weighting.ts, revocation.ts, recovery.ts, wallet.ts all benefit from the new semantics; none break. The version bump prevents a future fresh-upstream-pull from silently reverting the patch.

outcome.tests_passing: 74 of 78 — the 4 failures are baseline (ots-codec parsing a UTF-8-corrupted fixture), unrelated to this change; verified by stashing changes and re-running
outcome.notes: Two commits pushed to claude/compare-library-wallet-OW5FF: a8e9b09 (sign-poisoning fix + tests) and 9d1a131 (version bump). typecheck / lint / build all green on tapit-attest. The ots-codec fixture test/fixtures/authorship-record.ots is corrupted at rest — bytes 0xbf 0x89 ... became UTF-8 replacement-character runs 0xef 0xbf 0xbd ..., almost certainly from web-upload bootstrap. Tracked as a separate-session task; out of scope here.

uncertainty: The two regression tests cover the documented attack vector cleanly, but the wider field-tree-and-anchoring path through verifyEnvelope has not been re-exercised since the semantic change. Existing test suite passing is reasonable assurance; a brief integration pass during Phase 2 would close the loop completely.
next: Operator decision: start Phase 1 (PWA shell + Supabase magic-link auth + key generation + encrypted snapshot) in the next session, OR request more design work first. My judgement is the former — DESIGN.md, DISCOVERY.md, and the now-patched library are sufficient context to begin cutting Phase 1.
